answer: To see what items customers added to their cart, go to Reports in your site's dashboard and open the Stores section. Use the Most Abandoned Products report to see products visitors placed in a cart but didn't buy, the Abandoned Carts Summary to study abandoned and recovered carts in detail (filterable by customer type, product value, etc.), or the Abandoned Carts Funnel to see how many carts were abandoned versus recovered. To see how items were sold, use the Sales by Product Variant report to see which product variants (e.g., size and color combinations) are selling the most, or go to your Sales reports and use Sales by item for a breakdown of specific items sold and Item sales over time to track sales trends for individual items.

To rename a web link (menu item) in the Wix Editor: Click Pages and Menu on the left side of the Editor. Hover over the relevant menu item and click the More Actions icon. Then choose Rename to change the name of the item on your site menu.

First, make sure you published your site after updating the og:image. Then use the appropriate debugging tool for the platform where you are sharing: for Facebook, enter your URL in the Facebook Debugger and click 'Fetch new information' (for URLs never shared before) or 'Scrape Again' (for URLs shared before); for LinkedIn, use the LinkedIn Post Inspector (https://www.linkedin.com/post-inspector/); for X use the X Card Validator; for Pinterest use the Pinterest Debugger. Note that LinkedIn may take up to a week to show updated information, and ensure your og:image uses an aspect ratio of 1.91:1 to avoid cropping issues.

To add a personalized name (or other dynamic values) to your automated emails in Wix Bookings: Go to Booking Settings in your site's dashboard, click Emails & SMS notifications, hover over the relevant automation and click Edit, then click Edit under Create an email. Click the text field where you want to add the name, click + Add Dynamic Value on the Customize text panel, select the relevant value from the drop-down (such as the client's name), optionally enter fallback text (e.g., 'valued client') for when no data is available, and click Add. You can also add dynamic values to the subject line by clicking Edit next to the subject and using + Dynamic Value. Finish by clicking Save & Continue, then Save.

Wix Stores is designed for selling physical and digital products (including dropshipping and print-on-demand items), not services. To sell services, the documentation points to Wix Bookings, which lets members book and pay for services online, and Wix Pricing Plans, which lets you charge for services, sell packages of services (e.g., a bundle of sessions), and offer memberships or subscriptions tied to services.

According to the documentation, Wix automatically creates a mobile-friendly version of your site using the content and elements from your desktop Editor, and all Wix Editor templates are responsive on different screen sizes. If your site is not displaying correctly on mobile, the documentation indicates this may be due to alignment or structural issues in the automatically optimized mobile view. For specific elements such as the Wix Pro Gallery, responsiveness in the Wix Editor depends on selecting certain layouts and setting the gallery to Full Width. The retrieved context does not include the specific step-by-step troubleshooting procedures for resolving general responsiveness issues.

This behavior typically occurs due to the image scaling settings on a strip background. If the image is set to 'Original Size', parts of it may be cut off. If it is set to 'Tile', the image is displayed in tile formation (repeated/multiplied) across the available space. To fix this, go to your editor, select the strip, click Change Strip Background, then click Settings. Under 'How's the image scaled?', select 'Scale to Fill' to resize the image to fill the available space without cutting it off or tiling it, then adjust the position using the 'Where is it positioned?' grid if needed.

A 403 Forbidden error means you are unauthorized to view the page you are trying to access. To resolve it: 1) Make sure the URL (web address) you entered is correct. 2) Clear your browser's cache and cookies. 3) Go to the web address you are trying to view again. If the problem persists, contact Wix support.

Unwanted gaps at the bottom of your desktop page can occur between the page content and the footer, or below the footer on the live site. To fix gaps between page content and the footer: select a different preset page design, or adjust the page height by clicking and dragging the Adjust Page Height icon (if your page is covered in strips, click and pull the footer down first to access the main page area). To fix gaps below the footer on the live site: change the page background color to match the footer color, add more content to the page to cover the viewport, resize the footer to make it longer, or check the Layers panel for hidden elements causing the gap.

If your dynamic list page shows items in the wrong order on the published site despite having sort conditions set in the dataset, check the following based on the documentation: 1) Ensure your site has been published since you added the dynamic page or made changes to the dataset settings. 2) Verify the dataset mode is set to 'Read' or 'Read & Write' — datasets in 'Write' mode cannot read collection content or apply sort conditions. 3) Confirm that the sort conditions are correctly applied to the specific field you want to sort by (e.g., the name/title field) and that the order is set to alphabetical (A-Z). Note that dataset sorts override any 'Mirror on Site' collection order, so the dataset sort should take precedence if configured correctly.

Users can check your calendar on your website by viewing the calendar app (such as the Google Event Calendar) that you have added to your site. They can see the events you have marked as visible to site visitors, displayed in the layout you selected (monthly, weekly, or agenda view), with details such as time zone and event start times shown according to your display settings.

If your subscription is in a grace period and recurring retries are enabled, the system automatically attempts to collect payment from the existing payment method (the same card) every 24 hours for the duration of the grace period. Alternatively, as a customer you can click 'Submit Payment' in the 'My Subscriptions' section of the Members Area and choose an existing payment method to retry the payment. As a site owner, you can also manually retry the payment by going to Subscriptions in the dashboard, selecting the subscription, clicking 'Collect Payment' > 'Submit payment', entering the customer's card details (with their permission), and confirming.

For a business Wix Payments account, your company's name and its registration number/tax ID (Company number) must match the company's registered information. If verification fails based on the Company number, re-enter the registration number/tax ID exactly as it appears on your company's registered information, and upload a company document that proves the validity and ownership of the VAT ID/Business ID/Tax ID/EIN during registration. The company document must have the tax ID/registration number visible and clear, the company name visible and clear and matching the business details in your Wix Payments account, and must have been issued within the last 12 months. Accepted formats are HEIC, JPEG, JPG, PDF, PNG (max 10 MB; min 1 KB for PDF, 100 KB for other formats). Also confirm that the Legal Business Name, Shareholder and VAT ID/Business ID/Tax ID/EIN entered in the form match those associated with your business bank account. Allow up to 7 business days for verification; if 7 business days have passed and the information is correct and matches your bank account details, contact Wix Customer Care.

To resize the image in your section: click the image and drag the handles on the edges to the size you want (using the corner handles keeps the original proportions). To add text to the image, click Add Elements on the left side of the Editor, click Box, and drag the container box onto the image; then make the box transparent by clicking Change Design > Customize Design > Fill Color & Opacity and dragging the Background slider to 0%, and drag your text element onto the container box. Alternatively, to add hover text (a tooltip) to the image, click the image, click the Settings icon, and enter your text in the 'Does this image have a tooltip?' field.

According to the documentation, menu item text should automatically sync: if you rename the page in the Pages & Menu panel, it automatically updates on your site menu, and renaming the item on the site menu automatically updates the Pages & Menu panel. However, the provided documentation does not include specific troubleshooting steps for resolving a glitch where the menu text fails to update.

The provided Wix Stores documentation does not describe a specific 'low stock' marking or alert feature. The available inventory management options are: (1) Tracking inventory by quantity (automatically updated on sale), or (2) manually setting status to 'In Stock' or 'Out of Stock'. To manage a shoe item's stock, you would either enter a specific quantity in the Inventory field or select In Stock/Out of Stock from the drop-down, but there is no documented 'low stock' threshold or label in the retrieved context.

After you create your campaign content, you send it to Google for review. If Google approves the campaign, it will run and appear as active; if there are issues, a "Disapproved" label appears next to the campaign with the reason, and you can fix and resubmit it. Regarding payment, your campaign is funded by a monthly subscription that is billed monthly (auto-renew) and applied directly to your ad credit each month, or by one-time payments for additional credits. You do not need to manually top up your credit unless you want extra ad credit beyond your subscription—the monthly subscription is automatically applied to your ad credits.

The provided documentation does not contain specific instructions for adding delivery information to a product page. The search results cover enabling delivery rate displays on the Cart Page and entering shipping information for Google Merchant Solutions, but do not address adding delivery information directly to the product page.

Wix Email Marketing can be used for free, but the number of emails you can send depends on your monthly balance. To send more emails per month, you must upgrade your email marketing plan. The retrieved documentation does not provide specific pricing amounts or plan tiers for the paid email marketing plans.

For a standalone image carried over from your desktop site, customization on mobile is limited: you can adjust the image's settings, crop it, and add an animation. To change the image settings on your mobile site, open the mobile editor, click the image, then click the Settings icon and choose from the available customization options (such as Reset Image Proportions and Image Behaviors). Note that the available settings for carried-over images do not include brightness/contrast adjustments, so if the image appears dark, you may need to edit the image itself (e.g., brighten it) before uploading, or crop/animate it on mobile to change how it displays.

The retrieved documentation does not specify the exact Meta Pixel events for Wix Bookings (e.g., service view or booking completed). It states that the Meta Pixel & CAPI integration sends all events automatically through the server and browser once connected, without additional setup, and references a list of pre-defined events by service that can be viewed when installing the integration, but the specific Wix Bookings event names are not included in the provided context.

The retrieved documentation does not contain specific information about changing your payment provider after funds have been sent for an order. The available docs only provide general steps to change providers (go to Accept Payments in your dashboard, click See More Payment Options, select a new provider, click Connect, and confirm the switch), without mentioning any restrictions or special procedures related to pending funds or completed orders.

According to Wix documentation, search engines take time to recognize that old URLs have changed or are no longer available, even after you submit an updated sitemap. Since you have already submitted your sitemap, you can speed up the removal of old URLs by using the URL removal tool in Google Search Console (this requires verifying your site with Google). You can also request indexing for your updated pages to encourage Google to re-crawl them. Keep in mind that Google must re-crawl your pages to detect the changes, so removal depends on when the search engines crawl your site.

Documents may be rejected for several specific reasons. For photo ID: it must be a color copy of an active, non-expired passport, driver's license, or government ID showing all 4 borders/corners, not blurry/overexposed/screenshot, with name and birth date matching your account details; for driver's licenses/ID cards, send separate files for each side; MRZ must be visible for passports. For bank documents (statement, voided check, or bank letter): they may be rejected if blurry, illegible, torn/damaged, rotated/upside down, a mobile screenshot, missing full account numbers, name/company doesn't match account details, account numbers are incorrect, it's a direct deposit form instead of a statement, or the voided check wasn't printed by a financial institution. Bank statements must be color, show the bank logo, full account number, and account holder name matching the Wix Payments account owner (or legal business name for business accounts), and be issued within the last 12 months. Address verification documents (e.g., utility bill) must be dated within the last 6 months, show one full page with clear name and address. All documents must be in HEIC, JPEG, JPG, PDF, or PNG format, max 10 MB (min 1 KB for PDF, 100 KB for others), and issued in the same country as your business location. If 7 business days have passed and you've confirmed all information matches your bank account details, contact Wix Customer Care to investigate.

Region or currency errors with Wix Payments typically occur because the currency set in your Wix account does not match the currency in your payment provider account, or because your business location/region is not supported by the provider. To resolve a currency mismatch: go to Settings in your site's dashboard, click Language & Region, scroll to Currency, select the currency that matches your payment provider account from the drop-down menu, and click Save. If you need to change the currency in your provider account instead, contact your payment provider directly. For region issues, verify that your business location (shown at the top right of Accept Payments) is correct and that your country is supported by your chosen provider (for example, Max supports Israel only, and PayPal is not available for businesses based in Russia).

To add a subscribe form to your site, the steps depend on whether you're using the Wix Editor or Wix ADI:

**Wix Editor (New Forms):**
1. Go to your editor and click **Add Elements** on the left side.
2. Click **Contact & Forms**.
3. Scroll down to the **Subscribe** section and drag a form onto your site.
4. Click **Settings** to customize layout, design, and manage submissions.

**Wix ADI:**
- **To add to a page:** Click **Add** on the top bar, click **Section to Page**, click **Subscribe**, and select the layout you want.
- **To add to your footer** (appears on all pages): Click the footer in the ADI builder and select the checkbox next to **Subscribe** on the left.

Once added, visitors who fill out the form are automatically added to your contact list with a 'Subscriber' label.

To update the terms & conditions checkbox at checkout in Wix Stores: Go to Checkout settings in your site's dashboard, click Policies, select the checkbox next to the policy you want to display, and enter the policy text. To make the checkbox mandatory for checkout, enable the 'Policy agreement checkbox' toggle. If you want the checkbox to be pre-checked by default, also select the 'Checked by default' checkbox.

Since you already followed the steps to set the Title tag in the SEO Panel and published, try these checks from the docs: 1) Remove any custom code you added to the site, as custom code can override the browser tab title. 2) Make sure you clicked Publish after entering the Title tag. 3) The change may be a local browser issue — open your live site in an Incognito/Private window, and if that fixes it, clear your browser cache and Wix cookies, then reopen the browser normally. 4) Note that if you haven't updated the page's title tag, the browser tab on your live site displays your site name instead. If it still doesn't work after these steps, contact Wix Customer Care with the troubleshooting steps you've taken and a screenshot/video of the issue.

Since you have a Google Workspace Admin account, you can reset the second business Gmail account's password as an admin. Sign in to your Google Admin account, click Password, then Reset Password. Choose to automatically generate the password or enter one yourself. Optionally click Preview to view it, and optionally enable the 'Ask for a password change at the next sign-in' toggle. Click Reset. You can then click 'Click to copy password' to paste it somewhere (such as a Google Chat conversation with the user), or choose to email the password to the user, then click Done.

To connect Google Analytics 4 (GA4) to your Wix site: 1) Create a GA4 property in your Google Analytics account using the GA4 Setup Assistant (Admin > GA4 Setup Assistant > Create property), then copy your Measurement ID from the Web stream details. 2) In your Wix site's dashboard, go to Marketing Integrations, click View under Google Analytics, click the Show More icon, then Edit. 3) Paste your GA4 Measurement ID (ensure no extra spaces), optionally select IP Anonymization, and click Save. Note: You must upgrade your site and connect a domain before using Marketing Integrations.

Your payments flow from your customer to your bank account through Wix Payments in three stages: (1) Processing payment — after a successful payment, funds go through a settlement period (usually 1-2 days) and a pending period (usually 2-5 business days) to protect against fraud; (2) Scheduled payout — the payment is added to your next scheduled daily, weekly, or monthly payout; (3) Sent payout — the payout is sent from Wix Payments and should arrive in your bank account within 3-5 business days. To receive payouts, your Wix Payments account must be verified and Active, and you need an available balance of at least $1. You can view previous and upcoming payouts, including detailed information about each payment and the Payout ID (which identifies the transfer to your bank account), by going to Payouts in your site's dashboard. In your payments table, the status will show as 'Paid Out' once the transaction was included in a previous payout to your bank account.

For a page without a footer, click the page itself and drag the Adjust Page Height handle at the bottom of the page to the desired position. Note: This option is only available if you selected the 'No Header & Footer' layout for that page. If the handle isn't moving, an element at the bottom of the page may be blocking it—you cannot make the page shorter if doing so would cut off an element. Move or delete the blocking element first (you can use the Layers panel to locate it), then try dragging the handle again.

It is not possible to edit or modify a domain name once it has been purchased. When you register a domain, you reserve the letters/characters in that order, so the only way to change your domain name (e.g., to remove 'DBT') is to register a new domain. Important: Domains purchased through Wix renew automatically, so you should turn off the auto-renewal option for the incorrect domain to avoid paying for another year.

According to the documentation, it is not possible to restore deleted Wix Stores products. While you can view and restore previous versions of your site in the Site History section, the docs explicitly state that 'it is not possible to restore certain page types such as Wix Stores products.' Additionally, CMS backups do not affect Wix App collections (including Wix Stores) because they get their content from the relevant app.

To sync your external calendar with Wix Hotels so visitors see correct availability, import your iCal URL into Wix Hotels (this is a one-way sync from your external iCal to the Wix calendar, blocking booked dates). Steps: 1) Locate your iCal URL. 2) Go to your Wix dashboard and click the Hotels tab. 3) Click to expand the Reservations tab and select iCal. 4) Click the Choose Type drop-down menu and select a room type. 5) Paste your iCal URL into the URL field. 6) (Optional) Click Add Calendar to add another room type and paste its iCal URL. 7) Click Save. Important: If you have multiple room types, you must add a different iCal URL for each room type. Note: This feature is not compatible with the Wix Hotels Channel Manager; if you want to use the Channel Manager, delete all URLs in this tab first.

To transfer an edited page from your duplicated (copy) site back to the original site, use the copy and paste page feature between the two Wix Editor sites. In the Editor of the copy site, click 'Menus & Pages' on the left side, right-click the page you want to transfer and select 'Copy'. Then open the Editor of your original site, right-click anywhere on the screen and select 'Paste' (or 'Paste & Apply Site Theme' to apply the original site's color and text themes). In the Pages panel, rename the new page if needed and click 'Done'. Note: You can only copy regular pages; you cannot copy anchors, links, folders, lightboxes, router pages, or pages from third-party and Wix business solution apps. The pasted page is always added as a main page to the target site's Site Menu.

To set one og:image for your entire site: open your site's settings, click Website settings, scroll down to General social image, click Upload Image, select an image (or click + Upload Media to upload a new one), click Choose File to add it, click Save at the top of the dashboard, then publish your site. The og:image is the image that appears when your page is shared on social networks (the docs reference Facebook, X, and other social networks, plus validators for Twitter, Pinterest, LinkedIn, and a note for WhatsApp). The retrieved documentation does not specify whether or how the og:image affects link previews in email or on Instagram, so that behavior is not confirmed by these docs. Recommended og:image specs: aspect ratio 1.91:1, 1200 x 630 px, under 8MB (minimum 200 x 200 px, recommended at least 600 x 315 px).

To transfer an edited page from a copy version to your original site without overwriting the original page, copy the page from the copy site and paste it into the original site as a new page. In the copy site's Editor, click Menus & Pages on the left, right-click the edited page, and select Copy. Then open the Editor of your original site, right-click anywhere on the screen, and select Paste (or Paste & Apply Site Theme if you want the original site's colors and fonts applied). The pasted page is added as a new main page in the original site's Site Menu, so your existing original page remains unchanged. You can then rename the pasted page by entering a new name in the Pages panel and clicking Done.

To download your website visit reports, go to All Reports in your site's dashboard, select the report you want, click the Download drop-down at the top right, and select a file format (Excel, CSV, or Image). To view data for a specific period such as December 15 to January 15, use the date picker drop-down at the top of the report to change the time period (the default is typically the last 30 days) before downloading.

To cancel within the 14-day money-back period: Go to Premium Subscriptions in your Wix account, click the More Actions icon next to the relevant plan, click Cancel Plan, then click Cancel Now to confirm. If you cancel within the first 14 days, your plan ends immediately and you are fully refunded (within up to 20 business days).

Wix offers 800+ pre-designed website templates that are carefully researched and curated by Wix designers to fit current trends and industry needs. You can choose from these templates to start your site, or use the AI site generator to create a personalized design. All templates are fully customizable using the Wix Editor's drag-and-drop interface. Additionally, if you see a ready-made design you like on a Wix template, you can save it to 'My Designs' in the editor to reuse across any site in your account.

To reassign a domain that is currently attached to a different site: Go to Domains in your Wix account and scroll to the relevant domain. Click the Domain Actions icon (or More Actions icon) on the right and select 'Assign to a Different Site'. Select the site you want and click Next. If that site is currently connected to a different domain, choose either 'Redirect it to the primary domain' (redirect your domain to the site's existing primary domain) or 'Replace the current primary domain' (connect your domain and disconnect the site's current domain), then click Assign.

You can use the third-party app 'Blocky: IP & Country Blocker by Effective Apps' from the Wix App Market. This app allows you to block visitors from certain countries from accessing your site, and you can immediately block multiple countries with a click of a button. After a visitor is blocked, they are automatically redirected to a page of your choice on your site. Note that this app is only available in English. For questions, contact Effective Apps directly at https://effectify.co/ or support@effectify.co.

The GPF/segmentation fault occurs when the GTK libraries are installed but are not at the specific required versions listed in the technote, even if newer 'latest' versions are present. The installed RPMs must match the minimum versions specified (e.g., gtk2-2.10.6-4.aix5.2.ppc.rpm, glib2-2.12.4-2.aix5.2.ppc.rpm, etc.). Alternatively, Installation Manager can be run without the GTK libraries by using console mode, command-line mode, or silent mode (with a response file), which do not require the GUI/GTK stack.

To remove the default compressed references (-Xcompressedrefs) on a 64-bit JVM, set -Xnocompressedrefs as a generic JVM argument for the WebSphere Application Server process. This removes the lower 4GB memory restriction on Class Pointers and Monitors/Locks, allowing native memory to grow beyond 4GB. Note that this will significantly increase Java heap memory requirements (it is not uncommon for 70% more heap space to be required), so you should adjust the Java heap size to a larger value and monitor/retune garbage collection as required. As a caution, before using this as a solution, rule out a native memory leak, since disabling compressed references allows native memory to grow unbounded.

When updating or configuring Decision Center (jrules-teamserver-<server>.ear) on WebSphere Application Server, ensure you do not change the class loading policies for applications and modules. Specifically, maintain 'parent last' class loading policy for all ODM modules. Changing these policies can cause ClassCastException errors during navigation in Decision Center.

Stop all WebSphere and related processes on the machine before running the installation. The IIM logs may show 'Running processes have been detected that may interfere with the current operation. Stop all WebSphere and related processes before continue.' Once all WebSphere processes are stopped, attempt the Portal install again.

The information is documented in IBM Security Bulletin swg21985013.txt. The bulletin states that IBM Integration Bus and WebSphere Message Broker, upon installation on Unix platforms, set incorrect permissions for an object (CVE-2016-0394, CVSS Base Score 4.0, Vector: CVSS:3.0/AV:L/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:L/A:N), which could allow a local attacker to manipulate certain files. Affected products include IBM Integration Bus V9 and WebSphere Message Broker V8. Remediation is available via APAR PI28139 in fix pack 9.0.0.4 for IIB V9 and fix pack 8.0.0.6 for WMB V8 (documented in swg21967265.txt). For current V8 or V9 fix pack installations on Unix, workarounds involve running specific chmod commands on the <IIB install dir>/isadc directory to set permissions to 755 for directories, 644 for files, and 755 for *.sh files.
The Sybase Server Agent 620 FP2 installer (6.2.0-TIV-ITM_SYB-FP0002) can be downloaded from IBM Passport Advantage using part number CNN25ML.

The Plug-in cannot locate the IBM Global Security Kit (GSKit) libraries required to initialize SSL, so it skips the HTTPS transport and logs the security library load errors. To resolve this on Linux, set the LD_LIBRARY_PATH environment variable to point to the GSKit library directory that ships with the Plug-in (for 64-bit Plug-in v8.x use: export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/opt/IBM/WebSphere/Plugins/gsk8/gsk8_64/lib64/). Because setting it only from the command line may not persist when the web server starts, add the export command to the web server environment file: for RHEL add it to /etc/sysconfig/httpd, and for SLES/SUSE add it to /usr/sbin/envvars. This allows the Plug-in to load the GSKit libraries and initialize the HTTPS transport.

This error indicates the temporary directory for extension points has become corrupted (this can happen after a server upgrade). To resolve without installing a fix: 1) Stop the WebSphere_Portal server. 2) Delete the contents of the directory: <wp_profile root>/temp/<node name>/WebSphere_Portal/_extensionregistry 3) Start the WebSphere_Portal server.

You can find the required authorizations by looking at the /IBMMON/AUTH profile available in the ITM transport imported into the SAP system. This profile contains the minimum required authorization settings. By examining this profile, you can obtain the complete set of authorization values needed to assign to your new custom userid (instead of the default IBMMON_AGENT) to ensure successful data collection by the MySAP agent.

Tune the sib.trm.linger property in the sib.properties file to adjust the messaging engine lookup delay that the Work Load Manager (WLM) uses before returning. The default value is 3 seconds, which corresponds to the 'Sleeping for 2999 ms' delay seen in the com.ibm.ws.sib.trm trace. Set this property in either <WAS_HOME>/properties (applies to all profiles) or <PROFILE_ROOT>/properties (applies to all servers in that profile; takes precedence if defined in both). After changing the property, restart the server for the change to take effect.

The transaction log gets corrupted when the IBM Content Collector server runs out of disk space, causing the IBM Content Collector Configuration Store Service to become hung and unresponsive to start or stop commands.

In a clustered environment, after deploying an updated ruleapp with 'Replace RuleApp Version', the previous version may still execute because the hot deployment notification was not sent by the RES console or not received by all Execution Units (XU) in the cluster. Other possible causes include: the user publishing the update lacking sufficient administrative rights (Monitor role in WebSphere Application Server) to notify all XUs through JMX; the updated ruleset failing to parse successfully causing the XU to fall back on an earlier active version; asynchronous ruleset parsing being enabled where an earlier version is used while the update is being parsed; or the ruleset update being written directly to persistence without triggering a notification. Validate that the requested ruleset path is correct and check that all cluster nodes received the deployment notification.

The clearing event is being dropped because the EIF probe on the OMNIbus side is resetting/closing (<RST>) the TCP/IP connection after receiving the event, so it never reaches the EIF logs or OMNIbus and the triggered event remains uncleared. To resolve this, set the connection_mode in om_tec.config on the ITM Server (TEMS) to connection_less instead of connection oriented: change 'ConnectionMode=co' to 'ConnectionMode=connection_less', then restart the EIF on the ITM using 'tacmd refreshTECinfo -t eif'.

The error is caused by an incompatible Windows security policy. Navigate to Control Panel > Administrative Tools > Local Security Policy > Security Settings > Local Policy > Security Options. Double-click 'System Cryptography: Use FIPS compliant algorithms for encryption, hashing, and signing' and disable it if enabled, then retry importing the keys. If the problem persists after disabling the option, contact IBM support for further assistance.

IBM Integration Bus Hypervisor Edition V9.0 and WebSphere Message Broker Hypervisor Edition V8.0 ship with Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL) Server 6.2, which is vulnerable to CVE-2017-14746, CVE-2017-15085, CVE-2017-15086, CVE-2017-15087, and CVE-2017-15275. Remediation: IBM strongly recommends contacting Red Hat to obtain and install fixes for Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL) Server 6.2, as applicable.

Yes. IBM WebSphere DataPower SOA Appliance can validate the signature of a Certificate Authority (CA) that signs a certificate using SHA-2 (SHA-256) while building the trust chain from the DataPower ValCred. This is supported on firmware versions 3.7.2, 3.7.3, 3.8, and 3.8.1.

The error IQQG0205E indicates a version incompatibility: the IBM FileNet Content Search Services client embedded in the IBM FileNet Content Platform Engine does not match the version of the IBM FileNet Content Search Services server. To resolve this, ensure the version of the Content Search Services client files included in the Content Platform Engine matches the Content Search Services server version. Check the readme files for your installed Content Platform Engine and Content Search Services fix packs for specific fix pack requirements (for example, Content Search Services 5.2.1.5 requires 5.2.1.5-P8CPE-FP005).

Look for the DATA #1 entry in the db2diag.log corruption message which contains the object identifier in the format Obj={pool:X;obj:Y;type:Z}. Here, pool is the Tablespace ID, obj is the Object ID, and type indicates the object type (0 = Table, 1 = Index). To find the object name, run the query: db2 "select char(tabname,20), char(tabschema,20) from syscat.tables where tableid=<ObjectID> and tbspaceid=<TablespaceID>". For example, for Obj={pool:3;obj:21;type:0}, run: db2 "select char(tabname,20), char(tabschema,20) from syscat.tables where tableid=21 and tbspaceid=3".

On a 64-bit JVM using compressed references, certain Java object data (such as class pointers and monitors/locks) must be allocated in the low-memory region (under 4GB) because the JVM reserves only 32-bit pointers for them. Even when the system has plenty of free memory overall, the OS memory allocator may exhaust this low-memory region first. When the JVM later attempts to allocate an artifact that requires low-memory, it fails and throws a Native OutOfMemoryError (NOOM). To resolve this, you can use the -Xmcrs parameter (available in Java 6.0.16.3, Java 6.1.8.3, Java 7.0.8.10, Java 7.1.2.10 and later) to increase the amount of low memory the JVM reserves at startup, or set -Xgc:preferredHeapBase to position the heap above the 4GB boundary. If NOOM persists, investigate application-level usage of Class Pointers and Monitors/Locks, and check ulimit settings for thread/process limits.

WebSphere Application Server is loading the JDBC driver class from the older ojdbc14.jar instead of the configured ojdbc6.jar because multiple versions of the same vendor's JDBC driver are present in the environment. When multiple versions of the JDBC driver are configured, irrespective of the scopes, there is a possibility of a collision of the classes and it cannot be predicted from which version of the driver jar the class got loaded. To resolve this, go to the JDBC Provider configuration and enable "Isolate this resource provider". When enabled, it ensures that only the jar specified in the classpath for that particular JDBC provider will be used for all datasources under it. This setting must be configured on each JDBC Provider; you cannot isolate only one resource provider.

This is controlled by the transaction timeout, not the HTTP session timeout. For Rule Team Server/Decision Center, the transaction timeout defaults to 10 minutes (600 seconds) via the `ilog.rules.teamserver.transaction.timeout` context-param in the teamserver web module's WEB-INF/web.xml (inside jrules-teamserver-<appserver>.ear\teamserver.war\WEB-INF). If a transactional operation while authoring takes longer than this, the transaction is rolled back and the user is effectively kicked out with a 'Transaction timed out' error. You can increase this value in web.xml. Also check the application server's container-level transaction timeout (for example, WebSphere Application Server 'Maximum transaction timeout'), which can also roll back long-running transactions.

This error occurs when changes to the setCenteraLibPath.sh (Linux/Unix) or setCenteraLibPath.bat (Windows) file are not picked up by the WebSphere Application Server startup script, typically because the Content Engine was restarted from within the WAS console rather than from the command line. To resolve, ensure the Centera SDK library path is correctly configured in the setCenteraLibPath script, then restart WebSphere from the command line (or ensure the script is properly included in setupcmdLine.sh) so the FPLibrary is found in java.library.path.

IBM Security Bulletin swg22004378 addresses CVE-2017-1557, a potential denial of service affecting IBM MQ channel processes. An authenticated user with authority to connect to a remote queue manager could send a specially crafted request causing the channel process to cease processing further requests, resulting in loss of service for other connections on the same channel (CVSS Base Score 4.3). Affected versions include IBM MQ and IBM MQ Appliance v8.0.0.0–v8.0.0.7, IBM MQ v9.0.0.0–v9.0.0.1 LTS, and IBM MQ/Appliance v9.0.1–v9.0.3 CD. Remediation requires applying Fix Pack 8.0.0.8, Fix Pack 9.0.0.2, or upgrading to IBM MQ 9.0.4 respectively. No workarounds are available. Full details are published in the IBM Security Bulletin at swg22004378.

The information is published in IBM Security Bulletin swg22003510 (with subsequent updates in swg22004378, swg22003852, swg21998663, and swg22012992), available via the IBM Secure Engineering Web Portal. CVE-2017-1236 describes a vulnerability where IBM MQ could allow an authenticated user to potentially cause a denial of service by issuing an incorrect saved channel status inquiry. The CVSS Base Score is 3.1 (Vector: CVSS:3.0/AV:N/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:L). Affected products include IBM MQ 9.0.2 Continuous Delivery, IBM MQ Appliance 9.0.x Continuous Delivery, IBM MQ 9.0 LTS, and various 8.0 and 9.0 maintenance levels. Remediation requires applying specific fix packs (e.g., 8.0.0.8, 9.0.0.2, 9.0.4, 9.0.0.3, or upgrading to 9.0.5 depending on the version). No workarounds or mitigations are available.

This is a known DB2 11 for z/OS defect documented in APAR PI19804. SQLCODE -401 from DSNXOBFC occurs when creating a native SQL procedure (such as CIUSNTSR) that contains a control statement with an IN-LIST predicate referencing SQL variables (e.g., IF variable IN (sqlvar1, sqlvar2)). DB2 does not process the SQL variables in the IN-LIST predicate properly, resulting in the incorrect SQLCODE -401 (operands not comparable) or potentially an ABEND. Apply the fix for APAR PI19804 (PTF UI20622) to resolve the issue.

The provided search results do not contain information addressing the specific issue of WAS runtime classpath not matching the WAS Server Runtime library in RAD causing NoClassDefFoundError at runtime. The retrieved documents discuss WAS packaging in RAD, 32-bit/64-bit editions, Portal file removal procedures, and WebSphere variables, but do not cover classpath mismatches between RAD compile-time and WAS runtime environments.

IBM SPSS Statistics Subscription (newer releases) is not supported on Mac OS X 10.9.5 (Mavericks). According to IBM documentation, OS X 10.9 is only supported for IBM SPSS Statistics 22 and only after applying FixPack 1; newer releases such as Statistics 24 require OS X 10.10 (Yosemite) through 10.12 (Sierra), and Statistics 25 requires macOS 10.12 (Sierra) or 10.13 (High Sierra). To resolve the 'installer not supported' error, you must upgrade your Mac operating system to a supported version (at least OS X 10.10 or later, depending on the specific SPSS Statistics version you are installing) or use an older compatible SPSS release that supports OS X 10.9.

This information is documented in IBM Security Bulletin technote swg22012983. The bulletin states that an IBM MQ client connecting to an MQ queue manager can cause a SIGSEGV in the queue manager's amqrmppa channel process, terminating it (CVE-2018-1371). Key details: CVSS Base Score 6.5, Vector (CVSS:3.0/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H), affected product is IBM MQ V8.0 at maintenance level 8.0.0.8. The current temporal score is available via IBM X-Force exchange (vulnerability 137771).

The error is caused by a corrupt installation of the CPE 5.2.1.2. To resolve this, re-install the CPE 5.2.1.2 .NET API: 1. Copy the software on a local disk. 2. Start the re-installation of the .NET API. 3. Select all sub-components of .NET framework 45 that were not listed before (select them all if unsure). During the next installation of ICC there are no further errors regarding missing components.

The retrieved documentation does not provide specific information about making the 'where' filter in Workplace XT My Inbox case insensitive. While one technote (swg21987296) mentions that for FileNet P8 repositories, setting the 'Force Case Insensitive Search' flag on the object store enables case insensitive searches in IBM Content Navigator (ICN), it does not address the specific behavior of the Workplace XT 'Tasks-->My Inbox--> Filter inbox based on field where' feature.

Theme files are served from the browser or proxy cache (HTTP 304) because the resolver uses a digest to cache URLs like resource aggregator collections, and this digest remains the same between restarts. To force the updated theme resources to load from the server, set the "digest.seed" key in the WP ConfigService to any string value. This generates a new digest on server boot, creating different URLs so the updated resources are served instead of the cached versions.

For IIB v10.0.0.9 and later, use the mqsichangeproperties command to generate a Java thread dump (javacore) against an execution group: mqsichangeproperties <Int.Node> -e <Int.Server> -o ComIbmInternalSupportManager/Java/JVM -n dump -v core. This produces a javacore file containing all Java threads running in the process. Alternatively, use -v all to produce a heapdump, javacore, and system dump. Dump files are output to $MQSI_WORKPATH/common/errors. Note that collecting Java core dumps is invasive and will impact the performance of the Integration Server process.
